cohort: Women with vertex-presenting, single, liveborn infants at term with persistent malposition in the second stage of labor (n=868)
finding: After adjusting for potential confounders, there was no difference between rotational instrumental delivery and cesarean delivery in the rates of delayed neonatal respiration, reported critical incidents, or low fetal arterial pH, but maternal blood loss was higher in the cesarean group.
mod_finding: Neonatal outcomes did not differ between rotational instrumental delivery and cesarean delivery once selection bias was accounted for.
